old: Chronicler Reporting: A krónikák szerint, úgy mondják
new: Chronicle Phrases: a krónikák szerint, úgy mondják
why: Screen taught evidentials (Unit 25) as a form: now presented as two fixed history phrases.

old: "title": "Attributing historical claims in Hungarian"
new: "title": "Two phrases for old sources"

old: When narrating medieval history, Hungarian frequently uses framing expressions like *a krónikák szerint* (according to the chronicles) or *azt mondják, hogy...* (it is said that...). This allows the speaker to report historical traditions without claiming direct eyewitness certainty.
new: Learn two fixed phrases for talking about the Middle Ages: *a krónikák szerint* (according to the chronicles) and *úgy mondják, hogy...* (it is said that...). They show that a statement comes from old sources or tradition, not from a witness. Treat them as set phrases here; *szerint* is taught as a pattern later in B1.
why: *azt mondják, hogy* is reported speech (Unit 25) and the evidentials are Unit 25; the screen now teaches phrases only.

old: értékálló aranyforintot veretett Körmöcbányán.
new: értékálló aranyforintot vezetett be.
why: *veretett* is a B2 causative (-tat/-tet).

old: Charles Robert minted stable gold florins in Körmöcbánya.
new: Charles Robert introduced a stable gold florin.
why: English of the same example (and the speaking screen).

old: Notice that *szerint* takes the nominative case (*a krónikák szerint*, *a történészek szerint*). It is an essential marker for natural historical and civic discussions.
new: Notice the word order: *a krónikák szerint* comes first, then the statement. You can swap in *a történészek szerint* (according to the historians).
why: A tip that called szerint a case rule; replaced by a phrase tip.

old: Diplomatic Reporting: megállapodtak abban, hogy...
new: Diplomatic Words: megállapodtak, egyezséget kötöttek
why: Screen taught cataphoric abban, hogy (B2); now a phrase list.

old: In diplomatic narration, agreements between rulers are introduced with prepositional verbs: *megállapodik vmiben* (to agree on something) followed by *abban, hogy...* (in that...). This pattern is central to describing historical treaties like the 1335 Congress of Visegrád.
new: To describe treaties like the 1335 Congress of Visegrád, learn these fixed phrases: *megállapodtak, hogy...* (they agreed that...), *egyezséget kötöttek* (they concluded an agreement), *közvetítő szerepet vállalt* (he took on the role of mediator) and *új utat nyitottak* (they opened a new route).
